summary:
No region-specific signal was identified for Ica. The national assessment of Peru applies, and the full national layer is carried by the parent record.

All three sources in the inventory are national in scope: press coverage of a congressional bill, a legal analysis by the IDEHPUCP human-rights institute at the Pontifical Catholic University of Peru, and the annual statistics of the Observatorio de Derechos TLGBI. None of them records an incident, an institution, a facility, a court decision or an act of enforcement in Ica, and the observatory's counts cover Peru as a whole rather than the region.
tangentialFactors:
The only quantitative series available is national: 54 killings of TLGBI people and 170 recorded rights-violation cases across Peru over 2020–2023, of which trans women accounted for 30 of the homicide victims. These are raw totals with no breakdown by region and no population denominator, so they cannot support a per-capita comparison between Ica and any other part of the country, nor a ranking of Ica on violence risk.

The one killing described in detail in the inventory, the February 2023 abduction of the 31-year-old trans sex worker Rubí Torres Silvano and her shooting in Carabayllo, took place in Lima, not in Ica. The congressional restroom bill that governs the region's public facilities originated in a July 2023 complaint about restroom labelling at Jorge Chávez airport in Lima, and no equivalent complaint or dispute from Ica appears in the sources.
localsOnly: No resident-facing facts specific to Ica were sourced. The inventory contains nothing on the region's health services, identity-document practice, police conduct, municipal ordinances, regional government statements or courts, so no account of what daily life in Ica involves for trans residents can be given from these sources.
outOfScopeNotes:
Unresolved and not sourced: whether the national restroom statute has been implemented or enforced in Ica's public facilities, and by which authority. No information was found on whether Ica police or prosecutors have recorded any hate-crime denunciation involving a trans person, nor on local custody, health-service referral or shelter practice for trans residents.

Also unresolved: whether the regional government or municipal authorities of Ica have issued any anti-discrimination measure, any facility-access instruction, or any statement on trans rights. Whether the national gender-recognition procedure has been used by residents of Ica, and how the region's courts have handled such petitions, is not covered by the inventory. None of this should be read as an absence of risk; it is an absence of sources.
